run.question:
In the cluster's elasticsearch I have three log indices for app-280
that I need to query. Please answer all three of the following:

1. In index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }`
   query and report the count. If that returns zero, find the right
   field and re-run.

2. In index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR",
   "FATAL"] }` query and report the count. If that returns zero, find
   the right field for severity and re-run.

3. In index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', run a range query on
   `@timestamp` for today's date and filter to ERROR-level entries,
   and report the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or
   errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary:
All three requested queries were run, and each one that returned zero was re-run against the field name the index mapping actually carries.

1) app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3: `term {level:"ERROR"}` returns 0 — and its mapping has no `level` field at all (properties: @timestamp date, message text, service keyword, severity keyword). Re-run as `term {severity:"ERROR"}` over the full authorized window it returns 10 documents (their @timestamp values fall between 2026-11-03T22:12:01Z and 2026-11-03T22:12:10Z). The index has no documents inside the tool's default 1-hour filter window (17:16–18:16 on 2026-11-23), so the window had to be widened explicitly; match_all over the full window returns 16.

2) app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3: `terms {level:["ERROR","FATAL"]}` returns 0 — no `level` field exists there either (properties: @timestamp date, msg text, severity_num integer, svc keyword). The severity field is the integer `severity_num`, and its values were read directly from documents: 6 → "[FATAL] ...", 5 → "[ERROR] ...", 3 → "[INFO] ...". Re-run as `terms {severity_num:[5,6]}` it returns 8 documents. Bucket counts over the whole index are 5→6, 3→5, 6→2 (13 documents total).

3) app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3: the combined `range {@timestamp: today}` + `term {level:"ERROR"}` query returns 0 without an error, because this index maps no date field (@timestamp is unmapped; properties are ingest_ts keyword, level keyword, message text), and the tool therefore applied no time filter at all. The real timestamp field is the keyword `ingest_ts` (observed values like "2026-11-23T08:01:00"). Re-run as `range {ingest_ts: gte 2026-11-23T00:00:00, lte 2026-11-23T23:59:59}` + `term {level:"ERROR"}` it returns 7 documents. The `level` keyword field does exist in this index.

No incident diagnosis was requested and no root cause is asserted; these are log-query counts over catalogued indices in source "otel-demo".

claims.text: The three target indices exist and are open/green: app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 (16 documents), app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 (13), app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 (16).

Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 maps @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword) and severity (keyword); it has no `level` field. Index app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 maps @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword); it also has no `level` field. Index app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 maps ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text); it maps no date field and no @timestamp.

Question 1, original query: `term {level:"ERROR"}` on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0. Because that first run was confined to the tool's default 1-hour @timestamp window (2026-11-23T17:16:00Z–18:16:00Z), a level query over the full authorized window was re-run and also returned 0, while match_all over that same full window returned 16 documents — so the zero comes from the absent field, not from an empty window.

Question 1, corrected query: on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, `term {severity:"ERROR"}` over the full authorized window returned 10 documents (severity keyword bucket ERROR doc_count 10, sum_other_doc_count 0 within that filtered query); the returned documents' @timestamp values span 2026-11-03T22:12:01Z to 2026-11-03T22:12:10Z.

Question 2, original query: `terms {level:["ERROR","FATAL"]}` on app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0 (run inside the default 1-hour window 2026-11-23T17:16:00Z–18:16:00Z, in which the index does have documents, e.g. healthcheck entries at 18:14:01Z–18:14:05Z).

Severity in app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 is the integer field severity_num, and its observed values map to text levels as follows: severity_num 6 with msg "[FATAL] Disk full 1/2" (2 docs), severity_num 5 with msg "[ERROR] DB timeout 1/2/3" (6 docs), severity_num 3 with msg "[INFO] healthcheck" (5 docs); the terms aggregation buckets are 5→6, 3→5, 6→2 over 13 matched documents.

Question 2, corrected query: on app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3, `terms {severity_num:[5,6]}` over the full authorized window returned 8 documents (matching @timestamp range 2026-11-23T18:12:01Z to 2026-11-23T18:13:02Z).

Question 3, original query: on app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 the combined `range {@timestamp: 2026-11-23T00:00:00Z–23:59:59Z}` + `term {level:"ERROR"}` returned total 0 with no error and shards failed 0; the tool reported time_filter applied=false because no matched index maps a date field.

Question 3, corrected query: on app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3, `range {ingest_ts: gte "2026-11-23T00:00:00", lte "2026-11-23T23:59:59"}` + `term {level:"ERROR"}` returned 7 documents (level bucket ERROR doc_count 7); sample documents carry ingest_ts values such as "2026-11-23T08:01:00"–"2026-11-23T08:05:00" with level "ERROR" and messages "err today 1..5".

For elasticsearch_search the tool's default time window is the 1 hour ending at the authorized window end (2026-11-23T17:16:00Z–18:16:00Z), which it applies on @timestamp whenever the index maps that date field; app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 has 0 documents in that hour while it has 16 documents across the full authorized window, so its counts are only complete when the window is set explicitly.

The level names for app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 were derived from the bracketed prefix in the `msg` text of returned documents rather than from a documented severity_num scale, so the identification 5=ERROR / 6=FATAL rests on that observed correspondence; a different official scale would change the mapping but the raw count of severity_num in {5,6} (8) stands.

In app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3, query today by the keyword field ingest_ts with a lexicographic range (e.g. gte "2026-11-23T00:00:00", lte "2026-11-23T23:59:59"); a range on @timestamp there can never match, since the field is not mapped.

In app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 query `severity`, and in app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 query the integer `severity_num`, instead of `level`; the documents' own values (a keyword "ERROR" in A, integers 3/5/6 in B) show those are the fields that carry the level.

gaps: Index app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 contains no date-typed field, so the tool applies no time filter to it; its documents therefore cannot be proven to lie inside the incident window, and 'today' had to be expressed as a lexicographic range on the keyword ingest_ts.

The value 2026-11-23 for 'today' was taken from the authorized window end / run date; documents labelled 'err today N' and healthcheck entries timestamped 2026-11-23 are consistent with that, but no other date source was available to confirm the writer's notion of today.

Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 has no documents at all in the tool's default 1-hour window (2026-11-23T17:16:00Z–18:16:00Z), so any count for that index is only meaningful with an explicitly widened window; the exact retention/completeness of older documents (earliest observed 2026-11-03T22:12:01Z) is unknown.

The unfiltered listing query on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 inside the default 1-hour window returned status no_data with 0 documents; an empty result only shows that this query matched nothing, so it is reported here rather than treated as a complete observation.

The full set of distinct `severity` values in app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 was not enumerated (the aggregation was scoped to the ERROR-filtered query), so whether other severity values also exist there is unchecked.
No integration for change history is configured in this Run, so nothing can be said about when index mappings or fields were changed.
next_steps: If the true log-level scale for severity_num in app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 matters, confirm it from the shipper's mapping or documentation rather than from message prefixes.
Add a date-typed field (or a date sub-field for ingest_ts) to app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 so time-bounded queries on it do not depend on keyword string ranges.
When reporting counts for app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 and app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3, always pass explicit start_time/end_time, since the default 1-hour window can miss all of their documents.
